title: perf(canary): improved auto-detection and rollout guards for performance canaries
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Recent incidents revealed gaps in automatic performance regression detection for our canary pipeline and insufficient hysteresis in rollout guards which caused noisy rollbacks. This PR improves canary auto-detection heuristics, adds hysteresis and burn-in windows to reduce flapping, and tightens the rollout guard policy integration with Smart Router so degradations trigger predictable fallbacks.

What I changed: consolidated detection rules into a single detector module, added moving-percentile latency detector, introduced configurable hysteresis and min-sample burn-in, extended rollout guard policy with per-route severity, and wired additional metrics to the canary reporting pipeline. Updated CI to run perf-canary checks in PRs and added unit + integration tests.

Why this approach: moving-percentile is more robust to traffic skew compared to simple mean/median thresholds; hysteresis + burn-in avoids noisy toggles during transient spikes; per-route severity enables safer rollouts for high-SLO routes and more aggressive rollouts for low-impact routes.

Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve existing thresholds; configuration keys are additive and can be rolled out via feature flags for Dedicated/Private.

Related: Linear ENG-2314, ENG-2978.
